Let D be actual disjoint free interior indices, E=I_free\D. Choose N as a fixed envelope of exterior free indices of original bare primitives meeting D; F=E\N. N must not depend on field values. Only original fine raw variables are varied, not coarse V or exterior V0.

With h=LMR1, b=LM2R1 require Rstar+2b+4<h so the entire source bad-indicator halos and changed S1 miss N. This is a sufficient geometric condition, not proof of analytic cutoff reorganization. L>11, M/M2>=L, floor(M/6)>=Rstar, R1>=1 imply this inequality: Rstar/h<=1/(6L), 2b/h<=2/L, 4/h<=2/(3L Rstar), hence sum<=17/(6L)<1 for Rstar>=1. Units and actual periodic partitions must agree. No actual tuple checked.

near_response_derivation: For an original local Wilson root with complete carrier S_p subset D, set u_p(n)=E_mu_n[M_p]. There is no direct n dependence in M_p under this carrier condition. Fixed compact real chart and fixed K_D justify differentiation under the integral.

For each j in N and unit block direction v, d_{n_j,v} u_p = -Cov_mu_n(M_p,d_{n_j,v} H). No hard inner-boundary flux is discarded: the original fixed-domain probability and existing reflected covariance theorem are used. A moving cutoff would invalidate this formula.
Let X_j=support_D grad_D(d_{n_j,v}H) subset N_R_H(j) intersect D. Full mixed Hessian column bound yields Lip_D(d_{n_j,v}H)<=J_H. If X_j empty the response is zero.

Ordered real unitary link products and original selected derivatives give Lip_D M_p<=g0 L_p, with a safe source-dependent L_p=4 c_Lie c_frame(1+K1) when those norm constants and selected slope bound are supplied. Inverse orientations preserve this bound. No numerical derivative constant or complex-background chart certified.

Write c_K=1 for real scalar roots and c_K=2 for complex scalar roots split into real and imaginary parts. Then ||d_{n_j}u_p|| <= (2 c_K/m) g0 L_p J_H exp(alpha R_H) exp[-alpha dist(S_p,j)]. Norm of complex response is bounded safely by the sum of the two real responses.

Let rho_N be the original per-block Euclidean cutoff radius including all norm-conversion factors; if the actual source ball gives rho_N=C_norm delta0/g0, keep that exact radius. Do not introduce a smaller cutoff.

Define H_half=sup_x sum_j exp[-alpha dist(x,j)/2] on the actual bounded-multiplicity fine graph. For d_p=dist(S_p,N), sum_{j in N} exp[-alpha dist(S_p,j)] <= |S_p| H_half exp[-alpha d_p/2]. Triangle/minimum distance and a union bound over S_p prove this estimate; H_half is finite in the actual fixed-dimensional graph.

If the actual K_N contains zero and all radial segments, define u_p^0(theta,F)=u_p(0). Integrating each block directional derivative on n(t)=t n gives |u_p(n)-u_p^0|<=A_p, where A_p=(2 c_K/m) g0 L_p J_H rho_N exp(alpha R_H) |S_p| H_half exp[-alpha d_p/2]. Oscillation between two arbitrary near fields is <=2A_p. This is a reference value in the same domain, not a new physical outer law.

When rho_N=C_norm delta0/g0, g0 rho_N=C_norm delta0. The smallness is at most O(delta0) with the displayed m,J_H,L_p,alpha,H_half factors; these may depend on the simultaneous parameter chain. No uniform decay/smallness conclusion follows without their actual common bounds.
outer_allocation: At fixed theta,F let pi_N be the actual positive normalized near marginal, retaining every exterior weight W_H and original normalizer. Put r_p=u_p-u_p^0, so |r_p|<=A_p. Arbitrary pi_N is allowed at this level; no mixing property of pi_N is asserted.

For bounded pure-exterior G(n), |Cov_pi_N(u_p,G)|=|Cov_pi_N(r_p,G)|<=2 A_p ||G||_infinity. Its transported exterior value is retained. A crossing root with direct n arguments needs the additional E_mu_n[d_n M] term and is NOT covered by the deep-root estimate.
For two deep roots, Cov_pi_N(u_p,u_q)=Cov_pi_N(r_p,r_q), hence absolute value <=2 A_p A_q, including complex bilinear covariance. The reference values are constants ONLY at fixed theta,F.

Law of total covariance at fixed theta,F gives |Cov_joint(D,N)(M_p,M_q)| <= (2 c_K^2/m) g0^2 L_p L_q exp[-alpha dist(S_p,S_q)] + 2 A_p A_q. The safe complex factor c_K^2 follows by four real covariance components.
There are two different distances: inner separation and depth from N. The boundary bridge does not give decay with root separation for roots near the boundary.

After integrating theta,F one must ADD Cov_{theta,F}(E[M_p|theta,F],E[M_q|theta,F]). Also u_p^0(theta,F) can depend on global U1 and history. This term is uncontrolled here. No cancellation of far/background/history covariance, no Rsc/Hsharp identification or unconditional connected physical theorem follows.
